newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: RESEARCH ALERT-Portuguese retailers a buy-Salomon.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Portuguese retailers a buy-Salomon.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said it recommended buying shares of Portuguese retailer Jeronimo Martins and Sonae Investimentos, whose retail activity is a core part of its business.
Salomon saw Jeronimo Martins posting a 45 percent rise in profits in 1998, while Sonae should reap great benefits from its Companhia Real Distribuicao (CRD) in Brazil.

In its August outlook, Salomon attributed strong profit growth to both an expected expansion in the Portuguese retail sector between 1997 and 1999 and the agggressive internationalisation of the two companies.
It put a 12-month price target of 14,200 escudos for Jeronimo Martins. The stock was trading at 11,910 on Monday.
The 12-month target for Sonae Investimentos was 8,850 escudos, compared with 7,450 escudos on Monday
Sonae's Modelo Continente, however, could underperform if it ends up without the Brazilian CRD which could stay in the hands of Sonae Investimentos, it said.
Salomon gave high marks to management at Jeronimo Martins and Sonae Investimentos.
"The skill of the Portuguese retailers in looking abroad is one of their comparative advantages over their Spanish equivalents," it said in the study.
